presets.name: Electric Dipole
presets.description: Two equal and opposite charges. Notice how field lines curve from + to −, and how the field on the perpendicular bisector points toward the negative charge.
whatToNotice: Field lines start on + and end on −
On the perpendicular bisector (y-axis), E points in the −x direction
Far from the dipole, the field falls off as 1/r³ (faster than a point charge!)

presets.name: Two Like Charges
presets.description: Two positive charges repel each other. There is a null point (E = 0) exactly between them.
whatToNotice: Field lines repel each other, curving away
At the midpoint, E = 0 (the fields cancel exactly)
The equipotential surfaces never cross

presets.name: Rod vs Disk Comparison
presets.description: Compare a finite rod (line charge) with a charged disk. On the axis, both show symmetry cancellation.
whatToNotice: On the perpendicular bisector, the component parallel to the rod cancels
Compare with a disk: similar symmetry argument applies
Far from the rod, it looks like a point charge

presets.name: Charged Ring - On Axis
presets.description: A uniformly charged ring. On the axis, only the axial component survives due to symmetry. At the center, E = 0.
whatToNotice: At the center of the ring, E = 0 (by symmetry!)
On the axis, all charge elements contribute equally to the axial component
The perpendicular components cancel in pairs

presets.name: Charged Disk - Near vs Far Field
presets.description: A uniformly charged disk. Near the disk, E approaches σ/(2ε₀) (like an infinite plane). Far away, it behaves like a point charge.
whatToNotice: Very close to the disk, the field is nearly uniform
Far from the disk, it looks like a point charge (E ∝ 1/r²)
The transition region shows the 'crossover' behavior

presets.name: Parallel Plate Capacitor
presets.description: Two parallel plates with opposite charges. The field is nearly uniform between the plates.
whatToNotice: Between the plates, E is nearly uniform (like superposition of two infinite planes)
Outside the plates, the fields largely cancel
Edge effects become significant near the plate boundaries

presets.name: Quadrupole Configuration
presets.description: Four charges in alternating arrangement. The field falls off as 1/r³ at large distances.
whatToNotice: The field pattern has four-fold symmetry
Field lines connect + to − charges
Far field falls off faster (1/r³) than dipole (1/r²) or monopole (1/r)

pedagogicalObjectives.symmetry: Understand how symmetry leads to component cancellation
pedagogicalObjectives.gradientRelation: E = −∇V: field lines are perpendicular to equipotentials
pedagogicalObjectives.nearVsFar: Near field behavior can differ dramatically from far field
pedagogicalObjectives.fieldLineRules: Field lines start on +, end on − (or infinity)
